title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Illegally Manufacturing, Trading, Transporting Firearms, Ammunition, Explosives, etc.

articles.content_en: Complete sets of firearm parts illegally manufactured, bought, sold, transported, mailed, stored, stolen, forcibly seized, possessed, privately harbored, or carried shall be counted as the corresponding number of firearms; non-complete sets of firearm parts shall be counted as one complete set of firearm parts for every thirty pieces.

The 'illegal storage' provided in Article 125, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law means the act of storing, on behalf of others, firearms or ammunition that one knows are illegally manufactured, bought, sold, transported, or mailed by others, or the act of illegally storing explosives.
The 'illegal possession' provided in Article 128, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law means the act of a person who does not meet the conditions for equipping or allocating firearms or ammunition, in violation of the provisions of laws and regulations on firearm management, taking possession of firearms or ammunition without authorization.
The 'private harboring' provided in Article 128, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law means the act of a person who is equipped or allocated with firearms or ammunition according to law, after the conditions for such equipping or allocation have been eliminated, in violation of the provisions of laws and regulations on firearm management, privately concealing the equipped or allocated firearms or ammunition and refusing to hand them over.

Where, due to normal production and living needs such as road construction, house building, well digging, or improvement of homesteads and land, or due to engaging in lawful production and business operations, anyone illegally manufactures, buys, sells, transports, mails, or stores explosives, and the quantity reaches the standards provided in Article 1 of this Interpretation, without causing serious social harm, and there is indeed a showing of repentance, a light punishment may, according to law, be imposed; where the circumstances are minor, punishment may be exempted.
Where the circumstances in the preceding paragraph exist, even if the quantity reaches the standards provided in Article 2 of this Interpretation, it may also not be determined as 'serious circumstances' provided in Article 125, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law.
Where explosives are illegally manufactured, bought, sold, transported, mailed, or stored in concentrated population areas such as public places or residential areas, or where, due to the illegal manufacturing, buying, selling, transporting, mailing, or storing of explosives, one has received two or more administrative penalties within three years and again commits the above acts, and the quantity reaches the standards provided in this Interpretation, the sentencing provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall not apply.

Where anyone commits acts such as illegally manufacturing, buying, selling, transporting, mailing, storing, stealing, forcibly seizing, possessing, or privately harboring other ammunition or explosive articles, punishment shall be imposed by reference to the conviction and sentencing standards provided in the relevant articles of this Interpretation.
